A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 17 pages of v3 and 20 pages of v4, including figures, equations, tables and appendices, support comparison despite substantial relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original confidence-estimation experiments on question answering and summarization, alongside sensitivity, feature-importance and cross-LLM transfer analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results in its main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The six perturbations, feature families and logistic confidence model remain. However, new Algorithm 6 uses entailment where the retained prose specifies contradiction, and Algorithm 7 shows one-way entailment where Section 3.2 requires mutual entailment. Whether these differences represent intended procedural changes or pseudocode errors is unresolved.

E1.justification: Both evaluate CoQA, SQuAD, TriviaQA, Natural Questions, CNN/Daily Mail and XSUM. Reasoning models are discussed only as a possible extension, without additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same baselines: semantic-set count, lexical similarity, eigenvalue, eccentricity, degree, semantic entropy and average verbalized confidence. This also holds for the matched-query and GPT-4-judge comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 permits SRC with at least two sentences; v4 Section 3.1 states that responses with fewer than three sentences are removed, although the two-sentence example remains. This is a limited reported preprocessing revision. Dataset splits, training sample counts, prompts and evaluation metrics remain unchanged; rerunning experiments is not established.

E4.justification: The decoding-count comparison, training-sample sensitivity, perturbation entailment check, feature rankings, transfer analyses and GPT-4-judge evaluation are retained. Several supporting tables move to Appendix B; the new Sample Efficiency heading introduces no new analysis.

E5.justification: Both state that results are averaged over five runs and that standard deviations for the proposed method are rounded to three decimal places. The corresponding uncertainty entries and reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All 15 tables retain their entries and values after matching renumbering and relocation. For example, SQuAD/Mistral AUROC remains 0.84 ± 0.003 in v3 Table 3 and v4 Table 2. The reported experimental findings are also retained.

T1.justification: Equation (1) and the prose definitions of semantic sets and confidence labels remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs, and v4 introduces no theoretical derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims of effective black-box confidence estimation, interpretable features and cross-LLM transfer remain unchanged. Adding ECE to the introduction and GPT-4 to the concluding model list restates evidence already present in v3.

C2.justification: v4 adds reasons for selecting the model architectures and conjectures that perturbations could affect reasoning models through their chain-of-thought outputs. It removes v3's explicit limitation that the English-only results might not generalize to other languages.

D1.justification: v4 newly identifies NLTK sentence splitting and spaCy named-entity recognition, and documents nucleus sampling and five split trials for SRC. The earlier NLTK stopword-source specification and sentence-permutation fallback for fewer than five eligible sentences are no longer stated.

R1.justification: v4 adds Chen et al.'s Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think and Raschka's Understanding Reasoning LLMs to support its new discussion. It removes Holtzman et al.'s decoding reference. The main related-work positioning is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: The methodology is substantially recast around seven pseudocode listings with revised explanations. Experiments are reorganized into separate Experiment Details and Results sections, with four setup subsections, a Sample Efficiency paragraph and a new Results appendix. Much of the findings prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn from a detailed feature-and-label schematic into a process flowchart. Seven algorithm displays are added, five main-text tables move to Appendix B, and the example and remaining results tables are repositioned. The matched table contents remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 improves navigation and supplies a clearer process diagram and additional implementation guidance. However, its new pseudocode conflicts with retained descriptions of SRC and semantic grouping, its sentence-length restriction is inconsistent with its example, and it removes the English-only limitation. With the empirical evidence unchanged, these documentation benefits and substantive ambiguities leave the net effect on overall quality unclear.
